questions.question: During insertion sort, why is `current = arr[i]` assigned before any shift?
options: To protect the value that shifts would overwrite
questions.explanation: Shifting copies earlier values to the right, including into index i, so the original value must be saved first.
optionFeedback: Sorting does not change array length.
Correct: current preserves the value being inserted.
Only the sorted prefix is involved in this pass.
A separate counter would count comparisons.

questions.question: After shifting stops with j at the last value smaller than current, where is current inserted?
questions.explanation: j ends immediately left of the gap, so the insertion position is j + 1.
optionFeedback: That moves two positions left of the gap.
j holds the last value that stays before current.
Correct: j + 1 is the opened cell.
The gap is not necessarily after the original position.

questions.question: Which condition makes the taught insertion sort descending?
questions.explanation: For descending order, smaller prefix values shift right so larger current values move left.
optionFeedback: Correct: shift a smaller value out of the way.
Shifting only equal values does not order the array.
That is a boundary state, not the order comparison.

questions.question: Why is insertion sort O(n) on already sorted input?
options: Each pass performs one failed order comparison and no shifts
questions.explanation: There are n-1 passes, but each inner loop stops immediately.
optionFeedback: The outer loop still visits each position after index 0.
Correct: constant work per pass gives linear total work.
The shown implementation uses a direct neighbour comparison.
